title: What Happens If You Skip Sleep for 11 Days?
sources: NPR, 'Lessons from sleeplessness: The 60th anniversary of Randy Gardner's world record' (2024-01-28) https://www.npr.org/2024/01/28/1227217274/sleep-deprivation-record (17-year-old Randy Gardner stayed awake 11 consecutive days, 264 hours, in January 1964; trouble repeating simple tongue twisters within the first days; marked cognitive impairment by days nine and ten; movement skills largely unaffected)

NPR, 'Eleven Days Without Sleep: The Haunting Effects Of A Record-Breaking Stunt' (transcript) https://www.npr.org/transcripts/562305141 and 'The Haunting Effects Of Going Days Without Sleep' (2017) https://www.npr.org/2017/12/27/573739653/the-haunting-effects-of-going-days-without-sleep (slept about 14 hours 43 minutes afterwards; felt 'groggy, but not any groggier than a normal person'; later developed insomnia he attributes to the stunt)

NPR book excerpt, 'Dreamland: Adventures in the Strange Science of Sleep' (2012) https://www.npr.org/2012/08/03/158087291/excerpt-dreamland-adventures-in-the-strange-science-of-sleep (memory loss and minor hallucinations by day four or five)
Scientific American, 'How Long Can Humans Stay Awake?' https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/how-long-can-humans-stay/ (Gardner was 'awake' but basically cognitively dysfunctional by the end)

Cleveland Clinic, 'Sleep Deprivation' https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/23970-sleep-deprivation (microsleeps = briefly falling asleep for only seconds before waking back up; trouble thinking, focusing and remembering; visual and tactile hallucinations in severe stages)

lines.text: Eleven days without sleep. What happens?
In nineteen sixty-four, a seventeen-year-old named Randy actually tried it,
but the weirdest part is how fast he bounced back.
lines.caps: BUT THE *WEIRDEST | IS HOW *FAST | HE BOUNCED *BACK

lines.text: By day two, he couldn't say simple tongue twisters,
and that's when microsleeps kick in, tiny naps lasting just seconds.
By day five, he was seeing things that weren't there,
lines.caps: BY DAY *5 | HE WAS *SEEING | THINGS NOT *THERE

lines.text: and by the end, his brain was basically running on fumes.
Then he finally slept for about fourteen hours,
and woke up, in his words, no groggier than normal.
lines.caps: AND WOKE *UP | IN HIS *WORDS | NO *GROGGIER | THAN *NORMAL

lines.text: But years later, he got serious insomnia and blamed the stunt.
lines.caps: BUT YEARS *LATER | HE GOT *INSOMNIA | AND *BLAMED | THE *STUNT

lines.text: So eleven days awake? Hard pass.
